data.narrative:
Krevera is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Edward and Sebastian Schneeweiss that has raised $3M+. The valuation analysis draws on a broader comp universe of 9 private robotics and manufacturing companies—including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI—plus 1 public comparable (277810.KQ).

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here. Using the $3M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to Series A, the analysis implies a valuation of $8M. A sensitivity range of $6M (low) to $9M (high) captures reasonable variance around this midpoint.

Peer-median triangulation does not yield reliable results. While 11 robotics and manufacturing peers exist in the dataset, the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar valuation tier—return insufficient overlap (fewer than three datapoints). Applying an all-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise given the specificity of seed-stage robotics. The single applicable method therefore anchors the range to $8M median, with key uncertainties residing in capital efficiency relative to peers, product-market validation milestones, and competitive positioning within a 9-company private peer set.
